proposal.utterance: What BFO category best fits 'the normative force of an obligation'?

entities.label: NormativeForce
entities.rationale: Normative force is the capacity of an obligation to bind, direct, or compel behaviour. It is internally grounded in the obligation (or its bearer) and is not yet actualized merely by existing — it is realized when the bearer acts in compliance or defiance. This matches BFO Disposition: a realizable entity that is internally grounded in its bearer's structure and is not a role (which requires external grounding). It is distinct from the quality of 'having an obligation' (which would be a Quality or Role) and from the process of complying. LegalObligation already exists as a working class (BFO_0000023/Role); NormativeForce is a distinct, finer-grained concept — the dispositional power that inheres in the obligation or its institutional bearer, realized in acts of compliance, enforcement, or resistance.

relations.rationale: NormativeForce is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016): it is internally grounded in the bearer (an obligation-bearing entity or the obligation itself as a generically dependent continuant), capable of being realized in behavioural or institutional processes.

open_questions: Should NormativeForce inhere in the obligation-bearing agent (a person or institution — a material entity) or in the LegalObligation role itself (a specifically dependent continuant)? BFO requires dispositions to inhere in material entities; if the bearer is the role, we need an intermediate bearer.
Is 'normative force' being treated here as a type (class) applicable to any obligation, or as a specific individual instance (e.g., the normative force of a particular statute's obligation)?
Should NormativeForce be modeled as a subtype of the existing working:LegalLegitimacyCondition (Disposition) or kept orthogonal to it?

Is there a distinction intended between normative force as a dispositional capacity (Disposition) and the felt or recognised quality of bindingness (which might be better typed as Quality, BFO_0000019)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The normative force of an obligation is best typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than a Quality, Role, or Process. A Disposition in BFO is a realizable specifically dependent continuant that is internally grounded in its bearer and whose existence does not require actualization — it can be realized in a process (here: acts of compliance, enforcement, or resistance) but need not be. Normative force fits this profile: it is the binding power or capacity that an obligation carries, inherent to its nature as an obligation, not merely an external relational property (which would favour Role) nor a static measurable feature (which would favour Quality). The existing working class LegalObligation is typed as a Role (BFO_0000023), capturing the externally-grounded status of being obligated; NormativeForce is a distinct, co-present dispositional aspect — the 'grip' or 'pull' of that obligation — and warrants a new class under Disposition. The key open question is what the proximate material bearer of this disposition is, since BFO dispositions must ultimately inhere in a material entity.
